title: RAG handbook
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines document retrieval with answer generation. A production RAG system needs ingestion, chunking, embeddings, a vector store, retrieval, reranking, and an answer generator. Hybrid retrieval merges vector similarity with BM25 lexical signals so that exact phrase matches are not lost.

title: Vector stores
text: Qdrant is a production-grade vector database that supports cosine similarity, filters, and durable storage. NurAI also ships an in-memory vector store useful for local development and tests. Chunk identifiers stored in Qdrant must be valid UUIDs so the cluster can deduplicate them.

title: Reranking
text: A reranker takes the top candidates from retrieval and reorders them based on stronger relevance signals. NurAI ships a lexical reranker that boosts results sharing tokens with the query, plus an optional cross-encoder reranker for higher accuracy at the cost of compute.

title: Evaluation
text: RAG evaluation typically tracks retrieval recall, answer relevance, and faithfulness. Ragas provides metric implementations on top of LangChain. NurAI also exposes network-free regression metrics so the eval suite can run inside CI without external API calls.

title: Operations
text: NurAI exposes Prometheus metrics, structured request logs, request IDs, an API key auth header, and a sliding-window rate limiter. The agent endpoint records a per-step trace so operators can inspect each LangGraph node decision.
